messages.text: I get the gist of it but please translate anyway, they're saying they want blood right?

[redacted:third-party-name], close—but not quite bloodthirsty.

[redacted:third-party-name] the translation of that message from [redacted:third-party-name] slang into standard [redacted:third-party-name]:

> "[redacted:third-party-name] of being sanguine, [redacted:third-party-name] not feeling very bloody sanguine today. Give us a pint or two on the house, that’s it lads."

“Sanguine” has a double meaning—traditionally it refers to being optimistic or cheerful, but also relates to the “sanguine” temperament (linked to blood in old humoral theory). The speaker is saying they are *not* in a cheerful mood at all and just want a few drinks, ideally for free. The tone is weary, defeated, maybe jokingly dramatic.

So nah, not literal blood—just vibes, beer, and probably a bit of existential exhaustion.
